header:
Stay or switch?
The raise gap

lines.text: Stayed at your job? The typical base raise just lost to prices.
lines.say: Stayed at your job? The typical base raise just lost to prices.

lines.text: Today ADP said private employers added 86,000 jobs in October.
lines.say: Today, A D P said private employers added eighty-six thousand jobs in October.

lines.text: But look at pay: stayers got 3.0% more base pay, switchers got 4.8%.
lines.say: But look at pay. People who stayed got three percent more base pay, and switchers got four point eight.

lines.text: Meanwhile, prices rose 3.7% in the year through September.
lines.say: Meanwhile, prices rose three point seven percent in the year through September.

lines.text: Our math: 3.0% minus 3.7% puts stayers' base pay 0.7 points behind.
lines.say: By our math, a stayer's base raise is about seven tenths of a point behind prices.

lines.text: With bonuses and overtime, stayers got 4.4%, beating prices. Switchers got 7.6%, their fastest since March 2024.
lines.say: Add bonuses and overtime, and stayers got four point four, beating prices. Switchers got seven point six, their fastest since March twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: ADP's chief economist says switchers got bonuses, overtime and more hours.
lines.say: A D P's chief economist says switchers got bonuses, overtime and more hours.

lines.text: The simple check: your own raise versus 3.7% inflation.
lines.say: The simple check: your own raise versus three point seven percent.

lines.text: Next: the official jobs report Friday, and October prices Tuesday.
lines.say: Next, the official jobs report lands Friday, and October prices come Tuesday.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Stayed at your job? Your base raise trailed inflation
post.ig:
Stayed at your job? The typical base raise just lost to prices.
ADP: private employers added 86,000 jobs in October.
Base pay: job-stayers +3.0%, job-switchers +4.8% (year over year).
Inflation: 3.7% in the year through September (BLS). Our math: stayers' base pay is about 0.7 points behind.
With bonuses and overtime: stayers +4.4% (ahead of inflation), switchers +7.6%, switchers' fastest since March 2024.
Sources: ADP National Employment Report (Nov 4, 2026), BLS CPI (Oct 14, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
